normalization.title: A list is not a ballot verdict
normalization.overview: DOJ seeks to hold California ballots linked to a list of more than 20,000 likely noncitizens; California and Los Angeles County dispute the basis, and DOJ later announced charges against 28 listed people.
normalization.whyItMatters: Worth reading to separate a lead, an eligibility finding, ballot handling and potential official liability. Skip it for a live court result; no signed order was inspected at the October 19 cutoff.
normalization.ghostMeshTakeaway: DOJ describes layered screening and later charges, while recipient records and voter advocates identify serious false-match and ballot-rights risks. None establishes the full list or a crime by an official.
normalization.falsification: A signed California order, original charging papers, and a reviewable sample of list outcomes would change this assessment.
normalization.freshness: As of 2026-10-19 23:33 UTC. Filings, letters and charges are attributed to the parties. The latest signed order and charging instruments were not inspected. No video speech is used.

claims.proposition: The dispute began with an October 13 DOJ demand for temporary ballot segregation by October 15 at noon Eastern.
claims.assessment: Corroborated chronology from recipient records. The roughly two-day deadline was DOJ's demand to implement segregation. The Secretary objected to being expected to obtain and verify a statewide list in that period; she did not ask DOJ for a separate 48-hour review. The County says the letter and data carrier arrived October 13. The October 13 demand's exact complete wording is not transcribed here.
claims.limits: Corroborated chronology from recipient records. The roughly two-day deadline was DOJ's demand to implement segregation. The Secretary objected to being expected to obtain and verify a statewide list in that period; she did not ask DOJ for a separate 48-hour review. The County says the letter and data carrier arrived October 13. The October 13 demand's exact complete wording is not transcribed here.

claims.proposition: Los Angeles County said it did not open the USB drive hand delivered October 13 under its security protocols; Homeland Security Investigations then emailed an Excel copy October 14, which County staff say they reviewed cursorily.
claims.assessment: Corroborated as the County's first-hand account, not independently audited device or file access. The unopened USB does not mean the County had no access to the list; the cursory Excel review does not establish voter-level eligibility. No device, list, password, or individual data is reproduced here.
claims.limits: Corroborated as the County's first-hand account, not independently audited device or file access. The unopened USB does not mean the County had no access to the list; the cursory Excel review does not establish voter-level eligibility. No device, list, password, or individual data is reproduced here.

claims.proposition: DOJ's court case and its >20,000 figure concern people described as likely noncitizens on a registration list; the requested remedy includes setting aside ballots pending verification.
claims.assessment: Corroborated as DOJ's allegation and request. It is not a judicial finding, confirmed count of ineligible voters, count of cast unlawful votes, or finding against election officials. The complaint says investigating thousands before the election is infeasible. Public record in this packet lacks a voter-level validation sample.
claims.limits: Corroborated as DOJ's allegation and request. It is not a judicial finding, confirmed count of ineligible voters, count of cast unlawful votes, or finding against election officials. The complaint says investigating thousands before the election is infeasible. Public record in this packet lacks a voter-level validation sample.

claims.proposition: California rejected the segregation demand and said DOJ had not furnished its office the underlying list or matching method.
claims.assessment: Corroborated as California's position. The Secretary offers to evaluate proof and methodology if provided. Her Nevada analogy and her reading of a separate October 9 court order are advocacy and are not independently established by this packet.
claims.limits: Corroborated as California's position. The Secretary offers to evaluate proof and methodology if provided. Her Nevada analogy and her reading of a separate October 9 court order are advocacy and are not independently established by this packet.

claims.proposition: County counsel answered DOJ on October 15 after a cursory review of the emailed Excel list; counsel said it included addresses throughout California and lacked matching method or individualized evidence for a County ballot-handling change.
claims.assessment: Corroborated as the County's account and contested legal position. It counters claims that officials never examined any version of the list or received validated voter-level proof. Its cursory review cannot establish the list's error rate or adjudicate DOJ's nonpublic evidence.
claims.limits: Corroborated as the County's account and contested legal position. It counters claims that officials never examined any version of the list or received validated voter-level proof. Its cursory review cannot establish the list's error rate or adjudicate DOJ's nonpublic evidence.

claims.proposition: On October 16, DOJ warned County counsel of potential criminal exposure for knowingly counting ballots it associates with people it identified as noncitizens.
claims.assessment: Corroborated warning, disputed legal premise. The letter cites 18 U.S.C. §§2 and 611 and argues federal law requires temporary segregation. It also calls the list people DOJ reasonably believes are likely noncitizens on p. 1. Its later phrasing does not upgrade those matches to confirmed status. The letter is not an indictment or prosecution of an official or a court ruling.
claims.limits: Corroborated warning, disputed legal premise. The letter cites 18 U.S.C. §§2 and 611 and argues federal law requires temporary segregation. It also calls the list people DOJ reasonably believes are likely noncitizens on p. 1. Its later phrasing does not upgrade those matches to confirmed status. The letter is not an indictment or prosecution of an official or a court ruling.

claims.proposition: DOJ and California disagree on whether the requested ballot segregation and related list maintenance would be lawful.
claims.assessment: Corroborated dispute, legal merits unresolved here. DOJ says the NVRA 90-day rule covers systematic list programs, not individualized segregation, and says §611 and aiding/abetting law apply. California says ballot withholding could disenfranchise valid voters and conflict with federal/state requirements. A letter cannot settle the statutes' application; the packet lacks a controlling order in the California case.
claims.limits: Corroborated dispute, legal merits unresolved here. DOJ says the NVRA 90-day rule covers systematic list programs, not individualized segregation, and says §611 and aiding/abetting law apply. California says ballot withholding could disenfranchise valid voters and conflict with federal/state requirements. A letter cannot settle the statutes' application; the packet lacks a controlling order in the California case.

claims.proposition: After the episode, DOJ announced criminal charges against 28 people and the arrest of 11, and asserted that all 28 were on the disputed >20,000-name list.
claims.assessment: Verified as DOJ's new public allegation, not a conviction or independently examined charging instrument. The announcement concerns alleged past registration, voting, and naturalization conduct by listed individuals. It does not verify all 20,000 list entries, show a ballot cast in the upcoming November election, or charge an election official. DOJ's statement that California “refused to look” is in tension with County counsel's October 15 account of a cursory look at the emailed Excel copy; the requested comprehensive verification was not performed.
claims.limits: Verified as DOJ's new public allegation, not a conviction or independently examined charging instrument. The announcement concerns alleged past registration, voting, and naturalization conduct by listed individuals. It does not verify all 20,000 list entries, show a ballot cast in the upcoming November election, or charge an election official. DOJ's statement that California “refused to look” is in tension with County counsel's October 15 account of a cursory look at the emailed Excel copy; the requested comprehensive verification was not performed.

claims.proposition: LULAC and NAACP groups filed to intervene, arguing that segregation might harm eligible voters and that stale records may misidentify naturalized citizens.
claims.assessment: Verified filing and advocate position; not a granted motion or finding. It makes voter harm concrete as a litigated risk. It does not prove a given list entry is wrong, establish an error rate, or resolve federal authority.
claims.limits: Verified filing and advocate position; not a granted motion or finding. It makes voter harm concrete as a litigated risk. It does not prove a given list entry is wrong, establish an error rate, or resolve federal authority.

claims.proposition: DOJ says the October 9 D.C. vacatur does not foreclose its California case because DHS purchased a public file and did not use SAVE.
claims.assessment: Verified competing party positions, not a holding that the earlier order does or does not govern California. This directly qualifies the Secretary's applicability concern in DD-04 and DD-07.
claims.limits: Verified competing party positions, not a holding that the earlier order does or does not govern California. This directly qualifies the Secretary's applicability concern in DD-04 and DD-07.

claims.proposition: DOJ filed a memorandum supporting ex parte TRO relief and described further refinement of its voter leads.
claims.assessment: Verified motion filing and government argument, not a signed order or independent accuracy audit. It says more than 175,000 potential matches were narrowed to more than 20,000 with screens, manual and duplicate checks, and requests relief before November 3. Cited declarations, voter-level evidence, and error rates were not separately inspected. Its p. 12 wording about “28 arrested” conflicts with DOJ's same-day releases saying 28 charged and 11 arrested; use the releases for those counts.
